prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Root cause: after loading tokens from storage in OAuthClientProvider._initialize(), token_expiry_time is never computed from the token's expires_in, so is_token_valid() treats a stale/expired token as valid. prs.cluster_pick_reason: Smallest, single-purpose diff that fixes the root cause directly in _initialize() (compute token_expiry_time via update_token_expiry when expires_in is present) and ships a dedicated expired_tokens test fixture to cover it. #3251 makes the identical _initialize() fix but bundles in an unrelated optional oauth-metadata-loading change (via getattr/inspect duck-typing), inflating the diff and risking merge conflicts with #2492's metadata work. #2875 doesn't touch _initialize() at all — it only adds a refresh-token attempt on the reactive 401 path, so the proactive is_token_valid() check remains broken and every request still round-trips an expired token before the new workaround engages; it's a narrower, more complex patch for the same underlying defect.

prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3063 keys off `str(message.id)` and simply 400s when that string key is already in `_request_streams`. #3221 additionally introduces a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` helper (prefixing with `i:`/`s:`) because the existing `str(id)` scheme collapses JSON-RPC's distinct int `1` and string `"1"` ids into the same key — under #3063's fix alone, an in-flight numeric id `1` would incorrectly 409 a concurrent string id `"1"`, and a string id equal to `_GET_stream` could still collide with the standalone GET stream's routing slot. #3221's diff also swaps in the same key helper everywhere `_request_streams`/event-store keys are built, so the fix is applied uniformly rather than only at the new duplicate-check site. prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: MCPError subclasses (triggered by UrlElicitationRequiredError, issue #2431) are not pickle-safe: the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ calls cls(*self.args), but self.args is set by MCPError.__init__ to (code, message, data), which doesn't match subclass constructor signatures, raising TypeError on unpickle. prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: MCPError subclasses (triggered by UrlElicitationRequiredError, issue #2431) are not pickle-safe: the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ calls cls(*self.args), but self.args is set by MCPError.__init__ to (code, message, data), which doesn't match subclass constructor signatures, raising TypeError on unpickle. All three PRs add reconstruction logic to src/mcp/shared/exceptions.py to fix this. (3 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: 3262 implements __reduce__ once on the base MCPError class via a module-level _restore_mcp_error(error_type, args) that uses MCPError.__new__ + Exception.__init__ to restore the exact __dict__, covering every current and future MCPError subclass without per-subclass code. 2555 only overrides __reduce__ on UrlElicitationRequiredError itself, leaving other subclasses (e.g. NoBackChannelError) with the same unpickling bug. 2478 also adds a _restore_mcp_error helper, but it dispatches via an explicit 'if exc_type is UrlElicitationRequiredError' branch and reconstructs through from_error/from_error_data (a round trip through ErrorData), which requires updating the dispatch function for every new subclass with a custom constructor and can drop instance state not encoded in ErrorData. 3262's test file additionally imports and exercises NoBackChannelError alongside UrlElicitationRequiredError, demonstrating the fix generalizes across subclasses rather than covering only the one from #2431.

clusters.pick_reason: Most surgical fix: keeps the existing single anyio.Lock and only moves `response = yield request` (the outgoing protected request/response wait) outside the `async with self.context.lock` block, directly targeting the reported stall with minimal surface area. #3243 replaces the lock with two anyio.Semaphore instances (lock + a new flow_lock) and adds asynccontextmanager plumbing — a larger, riskier change with dual-lock ordering to reason about for the same end result. #2858 is a rebase of an older community PR tied to a separate issue (#2847), but its visible diff only contains an unrelated httpx2→httpx import cleanup, giving no verifiable evidence of the actual lock-narrowing implementation and higher risk of rebase conflicts from that same import churn already landing elsewhere.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys off `str(message.id)` and simply 400s when that string key is already in `_request_streams`. #3221 additionally introduces a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` helper (prefixing with `i:`/`s:`) because the existing `str(id)` scheme collapses JSON-RPC's distinct int `1` and string `"1"` ids into the same key — under #3063's fix alone, an in-flight numeric id `1` would incorrectly 409 a concurrent string id `"1"`, and a string id equal to `_GET_stream` could still collide with the standalone GET stream's routing slot. #3221's diff also swaps in the same key helper everywhere `_request_streams`/event-store keys are built, so the fix is applied uniformly rather than only at the new duplicate-check site. Net effect: #3221 covers every case #3063 covers plus the int/string collapsing and GET_STREAM_KEY collision edge cases it misses.

members.title: fix(streamable-http): reject duplicate in-flight request ids
members.author: Sammy-Dabbas
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3221: A second concurrent POST request reusing the same JSON-RPC request id overwrites the first request's slot in `_request_streams`, cross-wiring their responses (one request gets the other's payload, the other hangs). Both PRs add a check in `_handle_post_request` to reject the duplicate with an error instead of overwriting the slot.
